metric_rationale: In all chosen trial pairs, the first cue (which has the highest validity) strictly discriminates between Option A and Option B. Take The Best (TTB) will deterministically choose the option endorsed by this top cue, ignoring all other cues. In contrast, the Weighted Additive rule (WADD) integrates all cues, and since the sum of the less valid cues often exceeds the top cue in these specific compensatory trials, WADD will frequently choose the option that lacks the top cue. Therefore, the proportion of choices aligning with the top cue will be near 1.0 for TTB, but significantly lower for WADD.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Take The Best (TTB) heuristic specifically on 'conflict' trials. In these trials (e.g., A=[1,0,0,0] vs B=[0,1,1,1]), the single most valid discriminating cue points to one option, but the sum of the less valid cues points to the other. TTB will consistently choose the option favored by the single best cue, resulting in a high metric value. Conversely, the Weighted Additive (WADD) model integrates all cues, allowing the numerous lesser cues to outweigh the single best cue, resulting in a low metric value.
